newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania sets portfolio fee at up to 1.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Romania sets portfolio fee at up to 1.5 percent.

text.p: Romania's government and central bank will set every six months a tax on portfolio deals in the local capital market, which cannot exceed 1.5 percent, a government decree showed on Monday.

The decree on foreign investment, printed in Romania's official gazette which makes it effective, introduces a tax of up to 1.5 percent on each portfolio buying deal -- set by the central bank and the government's Reform Council. Previous proposals called for a fixed 1.5 percent fee.
The rules, seen as crucial for the expansion of the budding capital market, were demanded by Western lenders and long awaited by foreign investors.
Under the new rules, the tax -- charged from the buyer by the broker responsible for the deal -- should go to the state budget within 10 days of payment.
Failure to pay the tax on time will compel the broker who retained the fee to pay a penalty of 0.25 percent per day.
Profits and investments can be repatriated freely, in the hard currency in which the initial investment was made, the decree shows.
The central bank keeps watch and accounts on hard currency operations involved in foreign portfolio transactions.
The rules baffled foreign investors when initially announced earlier this month. They said the 1.5 percent tax was punitive in nature and made the Romanian market expensive.
But foreigners later gave their backing to the new rules, turning bullish on both the Bucharest bourse and the over-the-counter market.

Brokers said foreign investors had accepted the new tax as a feature of an emerging market, assuming it the way they have assumed currency risk. They also said the market had sufficient potential to render the fee bearable.
Romania's government plans to issue new rules for domestic portfolio investors, similar to the regulations for foreign investment in the local capital market.
